sentences.text: Learned APP waives service of notice of Rule for and on behalf of the respondent - State of Gujarat.

[1.0] By way of the present application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short "BNSS"), the applicant has prayed for anticipatory bail in the event of arrest in connection with the FIR being C.R. No. 11210055241319 of 2024 registered with Salabatpura Police Station, Surat, for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 420 and 114 of Indian Penal Code, 1860.
[2.0] Learned advocate for the applicant submits that the applicant has nothing to do with the offence.
The applicant has no past antecedent.
Dispute is commercial in nature and only with a view to recover the amount, FIR is filed belatedly after a period of 4 years.
He is ready and willing to join the investigation.
Therefore, custodial interrogation at this stage is not necessary.
Besides, the applicant is available during the course of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/9230/2025 ORDER DATED: 08/05/2025 undefined investigation and will not flee from justice.

In view of the above,
the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: [3.0] Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent - State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.
He has submitted that the investigation is at initial stage.

The applicant is very much named in FIR and has committed offence of cheating and criminal breach of trust, because he has purchased the goods on credit worth of Rs.6,15,317/- and initially made payment of Rs.30,354/-, however, did not make payment of Rs.5,84,963/-.
If he grants bail, possibility cannot be ruled out to tamper the evidence.

Therefore,
custodial interrogation is required.
Hence, application does not deserve any consideration.

[4.0] Having heard the learned advocate for the parties and perusing the investigation papers, it is equally incumbent upon the Court to exercise its discretion judiciously, cautiously and strictly in compliance with the basic principles laid down in a plethora of decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court on the point.

It is well settled that, among other circumstances, the factors to be borne in mind while considering an application for bail are (i) the nature and gravity of the accusation; (ii) the antecedents of the applicant including the fact as to whether he has previously undergone imprisonment on conviction by a Court in respect of any cognizable offence; (iii) the possibility of the applicant to flee from justice; and (iv) where the accusation has been made with the object of injuring or humiliating the applicant by having him so arrested.

Though at the stage of granting bail an elaborate NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/9230/2025 ORDER DATED: 08/05/2025 undefined examination of evidence and detailed reasons touching the merit of the case, which may prejudice the accused, should be avoided.
I have considered the following aspects.

(1) The applicant has no past antecedent;
(2) There is delay in registration of FIR;

(3) Allegation against the applicant is that, he is owner of Balaji Textile and after purchasing the goods on credit through one broker Dilipbhai Asava from 09.01.2020 and 11.03.2020, did not make payment of Rs.5,84,963/-.
To recover the said amount, complaint is filed; (4) No allegation of criminal breach of trust or cheating is there;

(5) Dispute is commercial in nature and for that, civil remedy is available;
(6) Applicant is ready and willing to join investigation; (7) Similarly situated co-accused considered by this Court.
